arguments.name: returns
arguments.text: A list/tuple/array of returns, a pandas Series (ideally with a DatetimeIndex), a one-column DataFrame, a CSV/Excel path, pasted table text, or a [`ReturnSeries`](#api-ReturnSeries) from [`load()`](#api-load).

arguments.name: benchmark
arguments.text: Optional benchmark returns in any of the same forms. Benchmark-relative metrics are computed only when a benchmark is supplied.

arguments.name: factors
arguments.text: Optional factor returns, one column per factor (a DataFrame, a CSV/Excel path or table text, e.g. Fama-French factors). A column named `RF` is the risk-free rate and is subtracted from fund returns. Factor-model metrics are computed only when factors are supplied; OpenFactsheet never downloads factor data.

arguments.name: name
arguments.text: Display name for the report.

arguments.name: return_scale
arguments.text: Declare `"decimal"` or `"percent"` only when automatic detection reports ambiguity. Applies to fund, benchmark and factors.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Declare the observation frequency of *undated* values. It is checked against dates when dates exist. Applies to fund, benchmark and factors.

topics.description: Analyze several return histories under one identical methodology.
topics.details:
Metrics are shown side by side; nothing is ranked. When the histories cover
different periods, an additional common-period analysis (the intersection of
all histories) is provided so that track-record differences are visible. The
same benchmark and factor returns, if supplied, are used for every investment.
topics.examples:
>>> comparison = ofs.compare({"Fund A": fund_a, "Fund B": fund_b, "ETF": etf})
>>> print(comparison.summary())
>>> comparison.table(common_period=True)

topics.name: Comparison

topics.description: The canonical OpenFactsheet report, returned by [`analyze()`](#api-analyze).
topics.details:
Every canonical metric is present, each with a status, confidence, warnings
and the assumptions it used. The report is a plain data object;
calculations know nothing about rendering, and every renderer (text,
Markdown, HTML, JSON) shows the same content. The report and every metric
in it link to the documentation of their own version (decision 0035).

topics.name: FactsheetReport

topics.description: Structured outcome of one metric (CLAUDE.md section 10).
topics.details:
`value` is `None` whenever the metric could not be validly computed, and
`reason` then says why. A non-finite value can never be stored. Every
result links to the page of the reference manual that defines it
(decision 0035).

fields.name: id
fields.text: Stable metric identifier (e.g. `sharpe_ratio`).

fields.name: name
fields.text: Display name.

fields.name: category
fields.text: Report section the metric belongs to.

fields.name: value
fields.text: Unrounded value (`float64`), or `None` with a `reason`.

fields.name: unit
fields.text: How to read the value (`decimal_return`, `ratio`, `fraction`, ...).

fields.name: status
fields.text: `applicable`, `low_confidence`, `supplementary`, `not_applicable`, `insufficient_data` or `error`.

fields.name: direction
fields.text: `higher_is_better`, `lower_is_better`, `context_dependent` or `neutral`.

fields.name: confidence
fields.text: Reliability of the estimate (`high`, `moderate`, `low`, `not_assessable`), never a judgement of the investment.

fields.name: nature
fields.text: `observed`, `derived`, `estimated` or `model_dependent`.

fields.name: observations
fields.text: Number of observations the value is based on (aligned observations for benchmark and factor metrics).

fields.name: formula_id
fields.text: Versioned formula identifier; it changes when the definition does.

fields.name: methodology_version
fields.text: Methodology the value was computed under.

fields.name: assumptions
fields.text: Canonical assumptions used, in words.

fields.name: warnings
fields.text: Data-quality and confidence warnings.

fields.name: reason
fields.text: Why there is no value, or why confidence was reduced.

fields.name: details
fields.text: Supporting quantities (intervals, dates, episode data, ...).

fields.name: reference_values
fields.text: Values from reference implementations, when recorded.

fields.name: documentation
fields.text: URL of the reference-manual topic defining this metric, for the version that produced the value.
